einzeiler: Comedian Kate Berlant talks about her HBO special Parmesan, phone addiction, and ghosts.
kurzfassung: Comedian and actress Kate Berlant joins the show to discuss her new HBO comedy special, Parmesan. The conversation explores her deep addiction to social media and phones, her experiences with coming out later in life, and her fascination with everyday absurdities like wedding speeches and awkward social interactions. They also touch upon her childhood growing up in Los Angeles with artistic parents and her memorable creative partnership with John Early.
stichpunkte: Kate Berlant's new comedy special Parmesan on HBO explores themes of superiority, certainty, and social media behavior.
Both Berlant and the host discuss the severe psychological toll of phone and social media addiction, noting how offline time restores personal intimacy.
Berlant shares her childhood background in Los Angeles as the only child of artistic parents, surrounded by abstract artists and avant-garde conversations.
The discussion covers her coming out later in life, her perspective on heterosexual relationships, and the shifting nature of sexual identity categories.
John Early makes an appearance via phone to recount their early friendship, living arrangements, and list of funny questions for Berlant.
Berlant reflects on physical comedy as a method of self-regulation and coping with anxiety on stage.
She shares amusing anecdotes about a disastrous chimney sweep encounter and an unnecessary medical angiogram triggered by excessive online research.
The episode concludes with observations on the unintentional humor found in wedding speeches and non-performers trying to act natural.

clips.hook: Meeting a peer who was already at the level of comedy idols
clips.text: John Early describes meeting Berlant in their twenties at a comedy show and immediately realizing she possessed the sophisticated comedic timing of a veteran performer in a mockumentary.

clips.hook: Attempting social media cleanses only to relapse immediately
clips.text: Berlant explains her repeated attempts to stop scrolling social media for weeks at a time, only to fall right back into the habit despite recognizing its toll on her mind.

clips.hook: A popular high school classmate warns that funny women scare men
clips.text: Recalling a formative teenage memory, Berlant shares how a cool classmate told her that men dislike funny women because it reminds them too much of competing with other men.

clips.hook: Finding out a sculpture-making father qualified her as a nepo baby
clips.text: Berlant expresses utter bewilderment upon discovering her inclusion in a magazine feature about nepotism simply because her father was a sculptor and her mother made a prop for Spinal Tap.

clips.hook: The exquisite theatricality of wedding speeches by non-performers
clips.text: Berlant explains that watching ordinary people deliver heavily structured and formulaic speeches at weddings provides her with the ultimate form of unintentional comedy.

beschreibung:
Kate Berlant was seeing a few too many ghosts for a while. Amy hangs with the actress and comedian and talks about why you can't have two class clowns in bed, if she's a nepo baby, and why all curses should be lifted for free.
